sessions.notes: Sets walled up and broke all at once. A few corners here and there but fast and difficult to get into. The model said 2.0 ft typical with 2.7 ft sets (waist high) and called it makeable: the typical size was about right, the SET size was out by roughly a factor of two, and the shape call was wrong in the way that matters.

morphology.label: Transverse bar and rip
morphology.bars: Bars running out from the beach at an angle, with rip channels between them.
morphology.waves: The good one. Defined peaks over each bar, corners either side, channels to paddle out through.
morphology.summary: Transverse bar and rip. Bars running out from the beach at an angle, with rip channels between them.
morphology.note: Wright & Short (1984) beach-state classification with the Masselink & Short (1993) tide-modified extension - the distilled result of years of daily visual observations of how waves break on sandbars. Driven here by an energy-weighted running mean of measured buoy conditions with a four-day half-life, because bars respond over weeks rather than hours. It is a statistical expectation, not a picture of this particular sandbar.

lastSkipped.reason: the outer transects are not dark in near-infrared, so this is not open water - cloud, haze, or a bad scene

sandbar.shape: The breaking line is running straight along the beach. A straight bar trips the whole wave at once, which is how closeouts happen here.
sandbar.note: Measured from 5 satellite passes. This is shown, not used: nothing on this page is computed from it yet. It gets a vote once there are enough passes to know how much a reading jumps around.
